report.summary: Chunk 10 of 11 of canary.py: contains run_canary, _new_run_id, dry_run_plan, load_history, append_history with docstrings and comments.
risks: dry_run_plan | medium | Docstring says 'Calls nothing -- no lane.ask is touched' but code does not call lane.ask, uncheckable if lane has other side effects. | Review lane.ask and other methods for side effects.
dry_run_plan | low | Docstring says 'Prompt sizes are computed by BUILDING a sample body' but sample is 'PLAN0000', not a typical probe body. | Verify that sample body is representative.

load_history | medium | Docstring says 'Corrupt and foreign-schema lines are dropped silently' but code drops lines with schema mismatch or invalid status, not foreign-schema per se. | Clarify docstring or adjust logic.
append_history | low | Docstring says 'Parents created; never rewritten' but code uses 'a' mode, which appends; parent creation is correct. | Confirm that file is never rewritten elsewhere.

handoff.purpose: Contains run_canary, _new_run_id, dry_run_plan, load_history, append_history functions.

symbols.name: run_canary
symbols.note: Starts threads for each lane, joins with timeout, collects results, returns CanaryRun.

symbols.name: _new_run_id
symbols.note: Generates a run ID from timestamp and random hex.

symbols.name: dry_run_plan
symbols.note: Returns a plan dict with lane/probe info, no external calls.

symbols.name: load_history
symbols.note: Reads JSONL history file, returns list of valid records.

symbols.name: append_history
symbols.note: Appends probe result records to JSONL file, creates parent dirs.

claims.why: Code does not call lane.ask or any external function; only constructs a dict.

claims.text: Prompt sizes are computed by BUILDING a sample body, so the plan reports the real payload rather than a guess about it.
claims.why: The sample 'PLAN0000' is used; whether that yields real payload depends on p.build(sample) which is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: A plan that shows the payload but not the bill is how ``--live`` becomes a surprise. Naming a seat reads only its identity properties, which are pure.
claims.why: Refers to live_egress_lanes and seat identity properties not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: Read the JSONL history, SKIPPING anything unreadable.
claims.why: Code skips lines that fail json.loads, are not dicts, have wrong schema, or invalid status.

claims.text: A half-written last line (the machine was rebooted mid-append) must not take the health check down -- a canary that crashes on its own log is worse than no canary.
claims.why: The try-except catches JSON decode errors from incomplete lines.

claims.text: Corrupt and foreign-schema lines are dropped silently and the rest of the file is still used.
claims.why: Corrupt lines cause JSON errors and are skipped; foreign-schema lines (schema != SCHEMA_VERSION) are skipped; valid lines are used.

claims.text: Append one record per probe result. Parents created; never rewritten.
claims.why: Code creates parent dirs with mkdir(parents=True), opens file in append mode, writes lines, never truncates.

observations.what: run_canary uses a list comprehension to collect results from plan, but plan is a list of tuples (lane, probe, box); box is a shared dict across threads; potential race condition on box['result'].
dry_run_plan uses a sample 'PLAN0000' to compute prompt sizes; this may not represent actual probe bodies.
load_history uses 'errors="replace"' when opening file, which could mask encoding issues; but docstring says corrupt lines are skipped.
append_history calls to_record on each result; to_record is not defined in this chunk.
